vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: qiaomai-skills
Version: 1.0.0

The QiaoMai Skills bundle is a comprehensive toolkit for AI agents, providing modules for multi-layered memory management (octo_memory.py), dynamic knowledge graphs (dynamic_kg.py), and task execution (smart_executor.py). The code is well-structured, follows standard programming patterns, and lacks any indicators of malicious intent such as data exfiltration, unauthorized network communication, or harmful prompt injection. The included scripts (e.g., publish_skillhub.py) are legitimate utilities for packaging the skill for distribution.

llm.summary: The skill's code and README advertise a full agent OS and ask for API keys/config in its documentation, but the registry metadata omits those requirements and the SKILL.md contains a prompt-injection signal (unicode control chars); these mismatches and hidden-character finding warrant caution and further review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (agent OS, memory, KG, executors) match the included Python modules (memory, dynamic_kg, executor, case_search etc.), but the package metadata declares no required env vars/config paths while SKILL.md describes ~/.qiaomai/config.yaml and several API keys — this inconsistency suggests the metadata is incomplete or inaccurate.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs to run qiaomai CLI commands, init wizard, start a dashboard (web server on a port), and to set API keys (OpenClaw token, Perplexity, Grok). It also contains detected unicode-control-chars (prompt-injection pattern). While the instructions don't explicitly tell the agent to read arbitrary unrelated host files, the presence of hidden control characters and broad, open-ended guidance (e.g., '一键配置向导', integrations) increases the risk of prompt-manipulation or unexpected behavior at runtime.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry shows no install spec (instruction-only), yet the bundle contains many Python modules and CLI scripts. That itself is not malicious, but it's an unusual combination: either the installer will deploy code that isn't declared, or the metadata is incomplete. No remote download URLs were declared in the metadata, which reduces obvious immediate risk, but the included scripts (publish_*.py) may perform network actions — they need review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md asks the user to export QIAOMAI_OPENCLAW_TOKEN, QIAOMAI_PERPLEXITY_KEY, and QIAOMAI_GROK_KEY (sensible for integrations) but the skill metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Requiring multiple API keys for different services is plausible for advertised integrations, but the omission from metadata is a red flag: the skill would access secrets that were not declared to the platform, and that discrepancy should be resolved before trusting keys to it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request elevated platform privileges in metadata. It does advertise persistent storage under ~/.qiaomai and starts a dashboard — normal for this kind of tool. No evidence in the provided excerpts that it attempts to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or provide API keys yet. Actions to take before trusting this skill: 1) Ask the publisher to reconcile metadata with SKILL.md (declare required env vars/config paths and an install spec). 2) Inspect the full scripts (publish_*.py, CLI entry qiaomai, and any network code) for network endpoints or uploads; search for HTTP/requests/urllib/socket usage. 3) Remove or display SKILL.md raw bytes to verify and eliminate hidden unicode control characters. 4) If you must test, run in an isolated sandbox/container with no real secrets and no access to sensitive files. 5) If integrations are needed, create limited-scope API keys and monitor outbound traffic. Full resolution (benign vs. malicious) would require a complete code review of the omitted/truncated files and confirmation from the owner that the metadata was accidentally incomplete.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Hidden/unicode control characters inside SKILL.md can be used for prompt-injection or to alter how downstream parsers interpret the instructions; this is not expected for a benign README and should be removed or explained.
